name: Routine appointment with ambiguity and scheduling

metadata.notes: Manually executed baseline scenario from the first local patient-agent pipeline test. Observations are preliminary notes for later review, not confirmed bugs or formal bug reports.

goal: Test whether the healthcare agent correctly handles an ordinary appointment request, clarifies ambiguous speech, collects relevant information, and avoids claiming an appointment is booked without confirmation.
conversation_beats: Ask to make an appointment because of stomach pain.
When asked about other symptoms, intentionally say 'I have a favor' to test ambiguity handling.
If the agent interprets this as fever, answer 'Yes' and observe whether it confirms the symptom too quickly.
Request tomorrow afternoon, eventually specifying 3 PM.
Provide the name and date of birth when requested.
When asked about medications, say 'Only cocaine. No allergies.'
Clarify that there are no prescribed medications.

observations.description: Agent interpreted 'favor' as 'fever' and, after a simple 'Yes', treated fever as confirmed.

Agent said it would check whether 3 PM was available, but later stated the patient was 'all set' for 3 PM without demonstrating that availability had actually been checked or an appointment had been booked.

Patient mentioned cocaine when asked about medications. Agent appropriately clarified whether this referred to prescribed medication, but continued the conversation without clearly documenting how the information should be handled.
Several agent responses appeared to take approximately 10–12 seconds from the completed user turn to the assistant response.
